injection.heldBody: The message may try to give orders to the agent. No agent has seen it, and agents cannot read it until you release it. Check the parts below — if it is harmless, release it.
injection.filterFailed: The prompt-injection filter failed on this message ({{error}}), so it went on unchecked.
injection.released: You released this message {{when}} after the prompt-injection filter held it (score {{score}}).
injection.suspiciousWarned: Suspicious phrases (score {{score}}, below the threshold {{threshold}}) — the agent was warned

reply.internalNote: Internal note about {{to}} — not a customer reply
reply.trustSenderTitle: Sends this reply and lets the agent answer {{to}} on its own from now on (Settings → Channels → the rule).
reply.trustSender: Send, then always for this sender

settings.mcpError: Agents cannot reply yet — registering the {{name}} MCP server failed: {{error}}
settings.injectionDescription: Every inbound message is checked before any agent sees it — e-mail (including text hidden in HTML), WhatsApp, webhooks and replies to agent tasks. A message that looks like an attempt to give the agent orders waits in the Inbox until you release it; agents cannot read it until then.
settings.holdDescription: On: a message under the threshold still reaches the agent, with a warning in its prompt when it looked suspicious. Off: nothing is checked or held; messages already held stay held until you release or ignore them.
settings.sensitivityDescription: Strict holds two medium signals together (more attacks caught; a mail about AI or prompts may wait for you). Normal holds only strong ones.
settings.autoApproveLabel: Agents set up channels without approval
settings.autoApproveDescription: On: accounts and rules an agent proposes are approved and switched on right away (safety checks such as sender filters for auto-replies still apply). Off: they wait for your Approve.

accountForm.label: Label
accountForm.gmailHint: Gmail needs an app password (Google account → Security → 2-step verification → App passwords).
accountForm.smtpHostHint: Optional; derived from the IMAP host.
accountForm.phoneNumberHint: Optional; used for the pairing-code method and to ignore your own messages.
accountForm.whatsappWarning: WhatsApp does not officially support linked-device automation. Use a secondary number if you can; a ban is rare but possible.
accountForm.replyUrlHint: Optional. Receives JSON decisions ({ id, action: reply or escalate, to, text, subject, inReplyTo }). Only reply goes to the customer; escalate is an internal handoff. Leave blank to poll results with the webhook token.
accountForm.allowEscalation: My application handles action=escalate as an internal notification, never as a customer reply
accountForm.callbackTokenHint: Optional. Sent as Authorization: Bearer to the Reply URL. Leave blank to keep the saved value.
accountForm.autoReplyAnyoneDescription: Lets rules of this account without a sender filter (e.g. a support mailbox) send the agent's replies without your approval. The agent still has no extra permissions; anyone who writes in can make it answer them.
accountForm.agentSendHint: Replies to inbound messages are governed by the rule that handled them; this covers everything else.

agentHelp.knowBody: Every agent has the {{mcp}} MCP server. {{getinfo}} gives it the full guide (accounts, rules, reply modes, prompt templates, webhook payloads) plus the live state of this instance. Just ask in a chat, e.g. “set yourself up to handle e-mails from @firma.cz in this project” or “create a webhook for n8n”.
agentHelp.proposalsTitle: Agent proposals need your approval (unless the switch above is on)
agentHelp.proposalsBody: Agents can propose accounts ({{proposeaccount}}: e-mail, WhatsApp, webhook) and rules ({{proposerule}}, defaulting to the agent’s project). A proposal shows up below as Proposed by an agent, stays disabled and does nothing until you press Approve — check permission mode, reply mode and senders first. The inbox badge counts waiting proposals. Agents never change or delete approved accounts and rules; they can only withdraw their own proposals. For WhatsApp the agent can hand you a pairing code after approval.
agentHelp.linksBody: Agents can put links into e-mails or messages for you ({{buildlink}}). A link opens CloudCLI with the prompt already typed into the composer — it is never sent on its own; you read it, edit it and send it. Several links in one e-mail work as ready-made actions (“Look at this e-mail and draft a reply”, “Offer a discount”, “Ask for the delivery address”).
agentHelp.linkSession: — continues that chat with its history (for an inbound message: the chat it started)
agentHelp.linksFooter: The prompt is URL-encoded, at most 4000 characters. You have to be signed in; a restricted user only opens their own projects. You can write such links by hand too, e.g. into bookmarks for prompts you use often.

proposal.title: Proposed by an agent · waiting for approval
proposal.hint: Disabled until approved. Check the settings above (Edit to change them), then approve.

rules.empty: No rules yet. Without a rule, messages land in the inbox and wait for you.

ruleEditor.name: Name
ruleEditor.sendersHint: One per line. E-mail, @domain.cz, +420…, or a glob like +420*. Empty = anyone: then the default permission mode only, and automatic replies only if the account allows replying to anyone.
ruleEditor.mentionsMe: In groups, only when my number is mentioned
ruleEditor.onMatchRun: Hand it to the agent right away
ruleEditor.onMatchHold: Wait in the Inbox until I send it to the agent
ruleEditor.conversationThread: Continue the same chat per thread
ruleEditor.conversationSender: Continue the same chat per sender
ruleEditor.autoReplySendersHint: One per line: an address or @domain.cz. The agent answers these senders right away, everyone else gets a draft. “Send, then always for this sender” on a draft adds to this list.
ruleEditor.promptTemplateHint: Leave empty for the default prompt. Placeholders: {{placeholders}}

validation.openPermission: A rule without a sender filter must keep the default permission mode: anyone who writes in would steer the agent. List the senders you trust to use another mode.
validation.openAutoReply: To reply automatically to anyone, pick one account above and switch on "Reply automatically to anyone" in that account's settings. Or keep drafts and list the senders to answer right away.
